result.summary: The intersection provides basic pedestrian infrastructure including marked crosswalks and sidewalks on all visible corners. However, the environment lacks dedicated pedestrian signal heads and modern traffic calming features like curb extensions to reduce crossing distance.

hazards.name: Missing Pedestrian Signals
hazards.description: No dedicated pedestrian signal heads are visible to provide clear crossing intervals.
hazards.location_in_image: At the intersection corners near the traffic light poles

hazards.name: Pavement Degradation
hazards.description: Cracking and wear in the asphalt within the crosswalk area could pose a minor trip hazard.
hazards.location_in_image: Foreground road surface and crosswalk area

interventions.title: Pedestrian Countdown Signals
interventions.description: Install dedicated pedestrian signal heads with countdown timers to improve crossing safety and clarity.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Add curb extensions (bulb-outs) to shorten the crossing distance and improve visibility between pedestrians and drivers.

result.summary: The intersection is equipped with high-visibility continental crosswalks and curb ramps, managed by overhead traffic signals. While basic pedestrian infrastructure is present, the wide crossing lacks physical protection like refuge islands or curb extensions to reduce exposure.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction
hazards.description: Parked vehicles on the left side of the street near the intersection may obstruct the sightlines between drivers and pedestrians entering the crosswalk.
hazards.location_in_image: Left curb line approaching the intersection

hazards.name: Unprotected Crossing Distance
hazards.description: The wide roadway requires pedestrians to cross multiple lanes without a median or refuge island, increasing exposure to traffic.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk at the corners to shorten the crossing distance and improve visibility by moving pedestrians past parked cars before they cross.

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Restrict parking within 20-30 feet of the crosswalk to ensure clear sightlines for both pedestrians and motorists.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Refuge Island
interventions.description: Install a raised island in the center of the roadway to provide a safe waiting area and allow pedestrians to cross one direction of traffic at a time.

result.summary: The image shows a signalized intersection with a marked zebra crosswalk and wide sidewalks. While basic infrastructure like curb ramps and traffic lights are present, the environment lacks dedicated pedestrian signals and suffers from sightline obstructions due to parked vehicles near the crossing.

hazards.name: Sightline Obstruction
hazards.description: Parked vehicles along the curb near the crosswalk obstruct the view between drivers and pedestrians.
hazards.location_in_image: Left and right curbs adjacent to the crosswalk

hazards.name: Lack of Pedestrian Signals
hazards.description: No dedicated walk/don't-walk signals are visible, forcing pedestrians to rely on vehicle traffic lights.

hazards.name: Pavement Degradation
hazards.description: Cracking and wear in the asphalt within the crosswalk area could present a minor trip hazard.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install bulb-outs to shorten the crossing distance and improve visibility between pedestrians and drivers.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Countdown Signals
interventions.description: Add dedicated pedestrian signal heads with countdown timers to provide clear crossing information.

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces immediately adjacent to the crosswalk to clear sightlines.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment features a wide, well-maintained sidewalk with a curb ramp and tactile warning surface. However, the crossing is uncontrolled and lacks high-visibility markings or signalization, requiring pedestrians to judge gaps in traffic on a multi-lane roadway.

hazards.name: Uncontrolled Crossing
hazards.description: Pedestrians must cross the roadway without the protection of a stop sign or traffic signal.

hazards.name: Standard Crosswalk Markings
hazards.description: The transverse line markings are less visible to approaching drivers than high-visibility patterns.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalk
interventions.description: Replace standard transverse lines with continental or ladder markings to improve driver awareness.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install bulb-outs to reduce the crossing distance and improve sightlines between pedestrians and motorists.

interventions.title: Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacons (RRFB)
interventions.description: Add pedestrian-activated flashing lights to the crossing signs to increase driver yield rates.
